As a General Attorney (Labor) (Resident Agent), GS-0905-14, your typical work assignments may include: Assignments requiring expedited preparation, intensive legal research, preparing detailed factual and legal reports and analyses involving factual and legal questions, conflicting legal precedents, controversial areas of labor relations, or other factors rendering resolution of difficult or sensitive cases.

Independently investigating and analyzing broad assignments by interviewing and obtaining affidavits from the parties and witnesses; reviewing and analyzing relevant records in order to make recommendations.

Engaging in: (1) making on-the- spot decisions and exercises judgment in unfair labor practice charge investigations, (2) unfair labor practice trials, (3) representation case investigations, (4) hearing officer in pre-election representation case, 10(k) investigations and hearings, post-election representation case proceedings, conducting bargaining unit elections, and when directed conducting analysis of Board Agent files.

In consultation with a supervisor, conducts federal court litigation involving injunctions under provisions of the National Labor Relations Act, as amended, and related proceedings involving the Board and its agents in the United States District Courts, civil in the United States District Courts and Courts of Appeals, subpoena enforcement proceedings, claims in bankruptcy proceedings, and other litigation in support of the Agency's compliance program.

Independently tries unfair labor practice cases before Administrative Law Judges, including examining and cross-examining witnesses, introducing evidence and exhibits, lodging appropriate objections, and arguing motions made by the parties, prepares post-hearing briefs or presents a closing oral argument to the Administrative Law Judge.

Making recommendations to the Regional Director concerning investigation and/or the settlement of unfair labor practice charges or whether representation cases should proceed, including examining the showing of interest presented in certain types of cases and negotiating appropriate Consent or Stipulated Election Agreements.
All qualifications and eligibility requirements must be met by the closing date of the announcement.

IDEAL CANDIDATE STATEMENT The ideal candidate for the General Attorney (Labor) (Resident Agent) will have experience preparing legal documents, including memoranda, motions, or briefs, and presenting arguments or making presentations on factual and legal issues. Knowledge of the National Labor Relations Act or similar related statutes is preferred.

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to interact with witnesses, opposing counsel, colleagues, and senior-level management; and strong research and analytical skills are desired. Must be flexible and willing to travel as needed to fulfill job responsibilities.

BASIC REQUIREMENTS Education: Must have successfully completed a full course of study in a school of law accredited by the American Bar Association (ABA) and have the first professional law degree (LL.B. or J.D.). Law school transcripts must be submitted at the time of application.

Bar Membership and Certification: Must currently be a member in good standing of the bar of a state, territory, or commonwealth of the United States, District of Columbia, or Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. Your active Bar license must reference Bar number and indicate the status of good standing.

Agency Internal Self-Certification Forms are not acceptable for verification.

In addition to the BASIC REQUIREMENTS, applicants must also meet the following: MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS Applicants must have one year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-13 grade level, which has provided them with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of a General Attorney (Labor) (Resident Agent) at the GS-14 grade level.

Specialized experience includes: Experience conducting legal research to identify and support the resolution of legal issues; and Experience working with labor, employment, or administrative law to render resolutions in cases; and Experience managing complex or sensitive cases with a high degree of independence.

This experience must be fully supported and articulated in your resume to receive consideration. Please do not cut and paste the specialized experience from this announcement into your resume, as this will not be considered a demonstration of your qualifications for this position.

NOTE: Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

(NOTE: All Agency employees must provide a copy of their SF-50 "Notice of Personnel Action" that indicates proof of status. The SF-50 must include your position, title, series, grade, step, tenure (1 or 2), and type of service (Excepted). As an employee, you may determine your status by checking block 24 on your SF-50.

The block must reflect "1" or "2". Also, block 34 must reflect "2").

About the Role: CrowdStrike is looking for a highly motivated attorney with extensive experience in executive compensation and equity matters to join our expanding corporate legal team.This individual will be a key liaison between the corporate legal, employment legal and HR functions and play a leading role in a wide range of workstreams, including in connection with CrowdStrike’s M&A transactions, compensation-related disclosures and equity incentive matters.

This position is open to candidates remotely in the USA. What You'll Do: Lead compensation and equity-related workstreams for M&A transactions, partnering closely with employment legal, HR and other teams to negotiate and drive alignment on key deal documents, manage due diligence, administer post-closing holdback arrangements and more.

Advise on compensation-related disclosures and corporate governance matters, including in connection with CrowdStrike’s proxy statement filings and annual meeting of stockholders.

Drive legal workstreams relating to CrowdStrike’s equity plans, including matters relating to ongoing plan maintenance, international expansion and the preparation of performance award agreements. Lead preparation and filing of registration statements on Form S-8 and support other filing workstreams as needed.

Advise on insider trading compliance and Rule 10b5-1 trading plan review and administration. Serve as primary legal point of contact for CrowdStrike’s stock administration function. Assist with compensation design, administration and compliance as needed.

What You’ll Need: J.D. and bar admitted with 7-10 years of relevant experience at a top-tier law firm and/or in-house at a public company. Deep technical expertise in executive compensation and global equity programs and associated M&A, disclosure and compliance workstreams. Meaningful experience working on complex cross-border M&A transactions.

Collaborative and proactive mindset with a “no task too big or too small” attitude. Excellent interpersonal skills, with a proven ability to establish strong working relationships and drive alignment across a broad range of internal stakeholders with competing priorities.

Outstanding organizational skills, with the ability to manage and prioritize amongst multiple high-stakes projects (e.g., M&A and proxy statement preparation) in an intense, fast-paced environment. Strong judgment and ability to balance legal risk with business needs.

Exceptional communication and presentation skills, with the ability to distill complex concepts into clear, actionable advice for various legal and non-legal stakeholders. Flexibility to work varying hours to accommodate global workforce, as needed. Bonus Points: Familiarity with Hart-Scott-Rodino (HSR) Act filings.

Serves as the UNC-Rear Attorney-Adviser for the Office of the Judge Advocate, Headquarters, United Nations Command in matters of International Law and U.S. Foreign Relations Law.
Advises the command on how U.S. law, customary international law, host nation law, and UNC equities may impact military policy, plans, operations, activities and initiatives of UNC in Japan.
Assists in the development and review of draft international agreements for the command.
Represents the command and its organizations on various commissions, committees, subcommittees, and other groups to discuss issues involving international law, host-nation relationships, and treaty commitments.
Participates in the developing, planning, and leading of negotiations undertaken by the command involving high level host-nation government officials.
Tactfully represents the command's position and endeavors to resolve differences involving serious conflicting interests.
Provides comprehensive legal services and support on various matters to include, but not limited to, international law, operational law, administrative law, labor and employment law, fiscal law, and claims.
Reviews existing, proposed, and amended legislation to identify and enhance the command's authority and scope of operations.
Who May Apply: US Citizens Applicants will be evaluated to determine if they meet the minimum qualification requirements and on the extent to which their application shows possession of the following knowledge, skills and abilities (KSAs) associated with the position.

KSA's: Skill in identifying and researching highly technical and complex legal issues. Skill in providing legal, technical, and policy guidance. Ability to effectively, professionally, and ethically manage a heavy caseload of clients with complex legal needs.

Qualification Requirements: The following minimum qualification requirements must be met before applicants are eligible for further consideration: Education Requirements: Position requires the possession of the first professional law degree (LL.B. or J.D.) AND active membership in the bar of the highest court of a State, U.S. commonwealth, U.S. territory, or the District of Columbia.

Applicants for initial appointment into attorney positions within the Department of Army must be graduates of law schools accredited by the American Bar Association at the time of the applicant's graduation. As indicated below, a law school transcript must be submitted with your application materials.

Bar Membership: Applicants must currently be a member in good standing (as defined by the pertinent bar) of the bar of the highest court of a State, U.S. territory, the District of Columbia, or Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. As noted below, proof of such membership and good standing must be submitted with your application materials.

Experience: In addition to the requirements above, applicants for the GS-14 or equivalent Attorney positions must also possess 3 years of professional legal experience, acquired after being admitted to the bar, commensurate with the duties and responsibilities of the position.

Graduation from an ABA-Accredited Law School in the top 25% of the class or an advanced law degree such as an LLM may substitute for one year of the required professional legal experience. Time in Grade: The Qualifying Authorities (QA's) will make a determination as to the applicability of time in grade based on the requirements of the position.

If you are currently employed as an attorney by the Federal government you must have completed one year at the next lower grade level within 30 days of the closing date of the announcement, or previously served at the same or higher grade level as the position being filled.

NOTICE OF VETERAN'S PREFERENCE: There is no formal rating system for applying veteran's preference to attorney appointments in the excepted service; however, the Department of the Defense considers veterans' preference eligibility a positive factor for attorney hiring.

Applicants eligible for veterans' preference must include that information in their cover letter or resume and attach supporting documentation (e.g., DD Form 214, "Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty") to their submissions.

Although the point-preference system is not used, applicants eligible to claim a 10-point preference must submit a Standard Form (SF) 15, "Application for 10-Point Veteran Preference", and supporting documentation required for the specific type of preference claimed.

The SF 15 will identify the supporting documentation required along with the list of the types of 10-point preference. The SF 15 is available from the OPM at https://www.gsa.gov/portal/forms/type/sf/.

Identify, research, and address extremely complex and difficult legal questions affecting United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) missions.
Represent the agency in administrative litigation, including matters before the Merit Systems Protection Board (MSPB), Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC), and Office of Special Counsel (OSC).
Counsel management on workplace issues, including harassment, misconduct, whistleblower protections, and professional standards of conduct.
Perform discovery, draft motions, prepare witnesses, and conduct hearings and appeals.
Who May Apply: US Citizens In order to qualify, you must meet the education and experience requirements described below.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document.

The minimum qualification requirements must be met before applicants are eligible for further consideration: Education Requirement: An applicant must have successfully completed a full course of study in a school of law accredited by the American Bar Association (ABA) and have the first professional law degree (LL.B. or JD.).

In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed below: Specialized Experience: Applicant must have three or more years of professional legal experience, acquired after being admitted to the bar, commensurate with the duties and responsibilities of the position.

Graduation from an ABA-Accredited Law School in the top 25% of the class or an advanced law degree such as an LLM may substitute for one year of the required professional legal experience. Professional legal experience includes: 1.

Research complex legal issues involving federal and state laws, regulations, and policies to provide authoritative legal guidance supporting organizational missions; 2. Prepare legal opinions, memoranda, contracts, and other legal instruments addressing complex or novel legal questions with significant programmatic impact; 3.

Represent the organization in negotiations, hearings, conferences, administrative litigation, and other legal proceedings with federal, state, local agencies, and private stakeholders; 4.

Provide legal advice and interpret federal, state, and local laws, regulations, and policies to support management decisions, policy development, and daily operations; and 5.

Conduct comprehensive legal research and develop legally sound recommendations to resolve high-impact matters involving significant financial, regulatory, or public interest considerations.

Bar membership: Applicant must currently be a member in good standing of the bar of a state, territory of the United States, District of Columbia, or Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. Fitness to Practice Law: An applicant must currently be fit to practice law.

If your fitness to practice law, or your conduct has ever been challenged you must submit a sworn statement giving the facts and circumstances, together with any explanations you consider appropriate. The sworn statement should be notarized and dated within 3 months of the date of your application.

(If you are currently employed as an attorney with The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, this requirement does not apply to you).

Time In Grade Requirement: If currently employed as an attorney by the Federal Government you must have completed 1 year at the next lower level within 30 days of the closing date of the announcement, or previously served at the same or higher grade as the position being filled.

Lyten is seeking to hire its first Patent & IP Counsel to build and lead the company's intellectual property function, with a focus on patent strategy, hands-on drafting and prosecution, and IP diligence across the company's product groups, including battery, concrete, composites, and sensors.

This is both a manager and a practitioner role: Lyten is looking for someone who will personally do some of the work of protecting its IP, not just direct outside counsel, as well as strategically manage and grow the company’s patent and IP portfolio.

This person will operate as an embedded business partner to product and engineering teams, not solely as a service provider, staying close enough to the technology and roadmap to shape patent strategy proactively and in accordance with the company’s core business objectives and strategic plans.

Key Responsibilities Own and drive Lyten's overall patent strategy and filing prioritization, developing technical fluency in Lyten's product lines and engaging with engineering and product teams on a recurring cadence to align decisions with the roadmap and competitive landscape.

Lead the company’s patent claim strategy with an eye toward the competitive landscape, and conduct or oversee freedom-to-operate (FTO) and infringement analyses for new products and acquisition targets.

Review and triage invention disclosures, determine what merits filing, and work directly with inventors/engineers to sharpen disclosures before moving to prosecution. Develop and manage Lyten’s yearly patent and IP budget.

Manage outside patent counsel and the patent prosecution docket across relevant jurisdictions; negotiate fee arrangements and control cost and quality of the outside IP spend.

Own patent portfolio strategy and hygiene: prune low-value applications and patents, maintain the IP docketing/management system, and keep the portfolio properly documented, assigned, and diligence-ready.

Review and negotiate certain complex IP provisions in commercial, collaboration, and research agreements, including ownership, licensing, and publication terms. Lead IP diligence on acquisitions and asset purchases, including resolving chain-of-title gaps and licensing ambiguities arising from M&A integration.

Advise on trademark strategy and enforcement, trade secret protection programs, and IP aspects of employment and contractor agreements (invention assignment, moral rights, and other jurisdiction-specific issues) across the business.

Coordinate with internal counsel on customer, supplier, and licensing IP issues, and manage the IP Consultant relationship and other outside IP resources, escalating specialized questions to outside counsel. Lean into legal matters outside core IP scope as needed to support the broader legal team given its lean size.

Required Qualifications J.D. and active license to practice law in at least one U.S. state; registration to practice before the USPTO required. 7+ years of IP experience, including personally drafting and prosecuting patent applications and setting patent filing strategy and prioritization (not just executing on an existing docket), with a track record as a practicing drafter rather than solely an outside-counsel manager, in-house or at a law firm supporting a technology/materials/hardware company.

Bachelor's degree in a relevant scientific/engineering discipline (materials science, chemistry, electrical engineering, or similar), given Lyten’s battery and materials technology. Demonstrated experience in competitive claim drafting and freedom-to-operate (FTO) or infringement analysis.

Experience with IP diligence in M&A or asset-purchase contexts. Strong drafting skills for licensing, collaboration, and confidentiality agreements. Preferred Qualifications Comfort using AI-assisted tools across the IP workflow, including invention identification, prior art/FTO search, drafting, and portfolio analytics.

Master's degree or Ph.D. in a relevant scientific/engineering discipline. Experience supporting an IP at a rapidly scaling company. Experience with battery, energy storage, or advanced materials patent portfolios. Experience with cross-border IP issues in international jurisdictions.

Experience with trademark prosecution and opposition proceedings before the USPTO. Familiarity with an IP management/docketing platform (e.g., Anaqua, CPI, PatSnap). Special Note U.S. citizenship required.

Protect Democracy is seeking an experienced, highly motivated attorney to join our team as Senior Counsel, focusing on the legal dimensions of artificial intelligence and advanced technology as they intersect with American democracy.

This role is integral to our scaling of the AI for Democracy Action Lab — Protect Democracy ’s multidisciplinary, nonpartisan “action tank” focusing on building tech tools and shaping law and policy to safeguard and strengthen democracy in the AI era.

This position is remote based in the US.* Please note: We are no longer hiring early-mid career Tech Counsel.

This is a position for candidates with at least 10 years of experience as an attorney, ideally including expertise in AI and emerging technology law, exceptional legal and analytical skills, entrepreneurial legal instincts, and a demonstrated ability to translate complex technical and legal questions for diverse audiences.

In this role, you will develop and advance legal strategies at the frontier of AI law and policy. From idea generation to execution, you will work with a small team driving creative impact litigation and other projects that integrate legal, regulatory, and communications strategies to constrain deployments of AI that are corrosive to our democracy.

You will also help build the AI for Democracy Action Lab’s expertise and credibility on the legal questions that will define how AI shapes our democracy. As a member of this team, you will shape the AI for Democracy Action Lab’s legal advocacy priorities, building upon the team’s strategies to date.

Our legal work has included advocacy to push back against the Pentagon’s retaliation against Anthropic for standing by its red lines, litigation challenging the administration’s attempt to chill online trust and safety work, and litigation and advocacy to stop the administration’s unlawful collection and aggregation of Americans’ personal data and deployment of technology for surveillance purposes.

At Protect Democracy , we believe that diversity isn’t just a strength — it’s a necessity for tackling the complex challenges facing democracy. A broad range of backgrounds, perspectives, and lived experiences strengthen our ability to analyze problems, craft solutions, and drive meaningful change.

We strongly encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds and from across the political and ideological spectrum to apply. If you meet most but not all of the criteria listed below but believe nonetheless you’d be a stellar match for the role and could grow into it, we want to hear from you.

In this role, you will: Identify, scope, and manage complex, high-stakes integrated advocacy projects to advance the AI for Democracy Action Lab’s goals; Lead and drive the development of innovative legal arguments and potential litigation approaches at the intersection of AI and democracy; Lead the process of researching, drafting, and editing pleadings, motions, briefs, and other legal filings in impact litigation; Lead communication with opposing counsel and manage and grow relationships with clients, coalition partners, experts, and government stakeholders in high-stakes litigation and non-litigation settings; Manage discovery processes, including informal fact-finding, document review, witness interviews, written discovery, depositions, and expert discovery; Supervise and mentor paralegals, junior legal staff, and law students; Write, publish, and present to key audiences on legal issues that gain significant traction at the intersection of AI and democratic governance; Brief reporters and provide expert commentary on complex legal questions and developments in AI law and regulation, serving as a public face for projects; Engage with policymakers, regulators, civil society partners, and the tech industry as a credible legal voice for pro-democracy AI governance.

Requirements The ideal candidate brings: At least 10 years of legal experience (which can include judicial clerkships), with expertise in AI and emerging technology law, exceptional legal and analytical skills, entrepreneurial legal instincts, and a demonstrated ability to translate complex technical and legal questions for diverse audiences; Bar membership in good standing in the jurisdiction of your residence; Experience developing and leading impact litigation or plaintiff-side civil litigation, including managing litigation teams for the senior role; Entrepreneurial legal instincts and an ability to generate impactful, creative ideas that advance the goals of the AI for Democracy Action Lab; Exceptional analytical, writing, and presentation skills directed at both legal and non-legal audiences; Ability to translate complex technical and legal questions for policymakers, journalists, and the public An embrace of a cross-ideological and nonpartisan approach to protecting our democracy; Growth mindset and enthusiasm for giving and receiving feedback up, down, and sideways; Collaborative orientation and willingness to take on tasks big or small as needed to advance our mission; Rigorous attention to detail and the highest standards for excellence in execution; A passionate commitment to the preservation of democratic norms and institutions, and an understanding that our democracy has never fully represented communities of color.

Compensation The starting salary range for this role is $170,000 to $193,000, commensurate with the candidate’s relevant experience, capabilities and skills and in alignment with internal equity. About Protect Democracy * Flexible location.

We are a remote-first organization based exclusively in the United States, meaning our staff work within the US and primarily virtually. We also offer shared workspaces for those who enjoy working in an office environment.

We are established for remote work in many states across the country, and while candidates based anywhere in the United States are welcome to apply, we may not be able to offer employment in your current location. If you proceed in the hiring process, we will discuss where you currently live and what is possible in our initial interview.

All staff are also required to travel at least two times per year to team retreats, and this role may require periodic travel. Accommodations to this requirement will be made only in exceptional circumstances. Commitment to an inclusive workplace. Protect Democracy is an equal opportunity employer.

We believe that a broad range of backgrounds, perspectives, and lived experiences strengthens our ability to analyze problems, craft solutions, and drive meaningful change.

Protect Democracy encourages applications from all qualified individuals without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, marital status, citizenship, disability, or veteran status. Phenomenal benefits.

Our benefits package includes generous sick leave and a flexible vacation policy where we encourage team members to take 4-5 weeks every year, along with 12 paid holidays, 6 weeks of paid family medical leave, and 18 weeks of paid parental leave. We also offer a 401(k) plan with up to 6% employer match that vests immediately.

Additionally, we cover employee medical premiums at 100% (with up to 95% coverage for dependents depending on plan selection), and employee and dependent’s dental/vision at 100%. All employees have access to long-term disability and life insurance, fertility benefits, a home office stipend, and bonuses at the discretion of the Executive Director.

To apply for this position, please complete the application linked below. You will be asked to upload your resume and cover letter as PDFs. Applications missing any of the required materials will be considered incomplete and not reviewed. Please note that interviews for this role will be conducted on a rolling basis.

Important notes Contact hiring@protectdemocracy.org if you require specific accommodations at any point in the hiring process. Keep an eye on your promotions/spam folders to avoid missed communication. We are unable to provide status updates for each application we receive.

If you reach out and do not hear back, please know it is not for lack of appreciation or interest, but simply for lack of staff capacity to respond to individual inquiries.

The application will include a voluntary EEO survey so that we can monitor the applicant pool as a whole for representation and equal employment opportunities, and to evaluate our progress as an organization toward a diverse and inclusive workforce, which we believe is a pillar of a thriving democracy.

The categories used by the EEO survey are limited and may not reflect your lived experience; please feel free to opt out of any of the questions. Your responses to this survey are entirely separate from your application materials, are not accessible to those responsible for hiring decisions, and will not affect your candidacy in any way.

Deine Rolle & Wie wir arbeiten Als unser (Senior) Legal Counsel (m/w/d) verantwortest du wichtige Teile der Rechtsfunktion von BIT Capital und bist die erste Adresse für alle (aufsichts-) rechtlichen Fragen.

Als von der BaFin beaufsichtigtes Institut bewegen wir uns in einem dicht regulierten Umfeld, welches bestimmt, wie wir Produkte auflegen, Portfolios steuern und mit unseren Investoren kommunizieren. Du übersetzt diese Anforderungen in Entscheidungen, die unsere Fachbereiche tatsächlich anwenden können. Du berichtest direkt an Dr.

Matthias Thom (Managing Director) und arbeitest in einem schlanken Set-up mit kurzen Entscheidungswegen.

s.h: In deiner Rolle fokussierst du dich auf
s.t:
Aufsichtsrecht. Du berätst unsere Fachbereiche eigenständig in allen aufsichtsrechtlichen Fragestellungen (WpIG, WpHG, KAGB, MaRisk, MaComp, GwG, DORA) und entwickelst unser Internes Kontroll- und Compliance-Management-System in der täglichen Anwendung weiter.
Erste Adresse im Haus. Du bist Ansprechpartner:in für Portfolio Management, Investment Operations, Sales, Marketing und HR und gibst pragmatische Handlungsempfehlungen statt Gutachten mit offenem Ausgang.
Prüfungen & Behördenkontakt. Du koordinierst in- und externe Prüfungen, führst die Kommunikation mit BaFin sowie Bundesbank und steuerst externe Kanzleien und Berater dort, wo wir spezialisierte Unterstützung brauchen.
Regulatorische Funktionen. Du übernimmst regulatorische Mandate, insbesondere die Rolle des stellvertretenden Geldwäschebeauftragten (Deputy MLRO) und des Datenschutzbeauftragten.
Neue Produkte & strategische Projekte. Du begleitest die Auflage neuer Fonds mit Kapitalverwaltungsgesellschaften und Depotbanken sowie unsere internationale Expansion rechtlich von der Struktur bis zur Umsetzung.
Verträge, Arbeits- und Datenschutzrecht. Du verantwortest das Vertragswesen und berätst in den weiteren Rechtsgebieten, die ein wachsender Asset Manager täglich berührt.
Deine Erfahrung Zwei juristische Staatsexamen mit überdurchschnittlichen Ergebnissen.
Mehrjährige Berufserfahrung im Aufsichtsrecht für Finanzinstitute, erworben in einer Großkanzlei, einer renommierten Boutique oder in-house bei einem regulierten Institut.
Sicherer Umgang mit den einschlägigen Regelwerken: WpIG, WpHG, KAGB, MaRisk, MaComp und GwG.
Belastbare Kenntnisse in weiteren Rechtsgebieten, insbesondere Vertrags-, Arbeits- und Datenschutzrecht.
Du erfasst komplexe aufsichtsrechtliche Sachverhalte schnell, entscheidest eigenständig und begleitest die Umsetzung federführend.
Bereitschaft, regulatorische Funktionen persönlich zu übernehmen und die damit verbundene Verantwortung zu tragen.
Du kommunizierst sicher auf Deutsch und Englisch.
2 Gründe dich nicht zu bewerben Du möchtest dich auf ein einzelnes Rechtsgebiet spezialisieren? Diese Rolle ist bewusst generalistisch angelegt: Neben dem aufsichtsrechtlichen Schwerpunkt liegen Vertrags-, Arbeits- und Datenschutzrecht ebenfalls bei dir.
Du arbeitest lieber im Kanzlei-Set-up mit Zuarbeit und mehreren Prüfschleifen? Bei uns bist du die Rechtsfunktion und triffst Entscheidungen selbst. Wir bieten dir dafür viel Gestaltungsfreiraum, unter anderem beim Aufbau einer Junior-Position an deiner Seite.
Dein Mindset Du besitzt eine Leidenschaft für Aktien, Finanzmärkte und Technologie.
Du verstehst Regulatorik als Fundament einer gesunden Organisation und nicht als Bremse. Du sagst klar, was geht, was nicht geht und unter welchen Bedingungen.
Du nutzt KI-Tools selbstverständlich in deinem Arbeitsalltag und denkst in deinem eigenen Aufgabengebiet konsequent an Automatisierung.
Du denkst unternehmerisch und bringst Dinge zu Ende, auch ohne perfekte Rahmenbedingungen. Ein reines 9-to-5-Mindset passt nicht zu dieser Rolle.
Was wir dir bieten Maßgebliche Verantwortung für die Rechtsfunktion eines wachsenden, BaFin-beaufsichtigten Asset Managers: Du gestaltest, statt zu verwalten.
Direkte Berichtslinie an Dr. Matthias Thom (Managing Director) und kurze Entscheidungswege in einem Team von 45+ Kolleg:innen aus 15 Nationen.
Tiefe Einblicke in Investment Operations und Portfolio Management und damit in die operativen Kernthemen der Finanzindustrie.
Perspektive, das Legal-Team mit aufzubauen, und ein Umfeld, in dem das Team signifikant in die eigenen Fonds investiert ist.

Passionate about making a difference and helping to make personalized medicine a reality through the use of data, Artificial Intelligence, machine learning and next generation genomic testing? Want to advise a cutting-edge business on novel legal issues at the intersection of healthcare and technology? Looking to transition to or expand in an in-house role at one of the most innovative companies in the world? Love counseling a business but want to know your work has meaning?
Genomic sequencing and other innovations in diagnostic testing permit us to decode and process our biological makeup. We now have more data than ever, but health care providers don't have the infrastructure or expertise to make sense of this data. We are on a mission to build and connect systems to redefine how healthcare data is used in clinical settings. We're looking to build a legal team that can support our ambitious business goals.
Location: Remote or Hybrid in Chicago

Your primary focus will be assisting with transactional work across our various business lines. Drafting. Editing. Negotiating. Explaining. Advising. Collaborating. The Legal Team handles complex commercial agreements of all types, all in service of our broader mission to help people live longer, healthier lives.
The agreements you will work on will be interesting - you will quickly be drafting and negotiating complex commercial agreements with both healthcare providers and life sciences companies.

You will work on an array of different types of agreements, including clinical and research projects, data license and transfer agreements, strategic collaborations, laboratory services agreements, agreements with payers, pharmaceutical companies, government entities and anyone else involved in healthcare, biotech and life sciences.

You will have to work through new legal issues involving artificial intelligence, large language models, intellectual property ownership, data privacy, and cutting edge healthcare technology. You will also work on common corporate contracts, such as vendor agreements.
In addition to this transactional focus, you will get a chance to grow and expand your skill set by assisting with other types of general legal work in a rapidly growing technology and health care company. Some areas you might focus on include intellectual property, employment and human resources, corporate governance, fundraising, mergers and acquisitions, regulatory, and international issues.
To do this job well, you will work with various internal business units, including our commercial organizations, data science, medical affairs, product & engineering, finance, communications, and our people teams. You will assist in evaluating legal risk and opportunities with the projects our businesses are engaged in, and help facilitate our business goals. We move fast, and we take pride that the Legal Department sets the pace.

Básico

This position is located in the Office of Chief Counsel, within the Legal Training Division in the Specialized Legal Branch at the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center. As a Attorney - Advisor (Instructor), GS-0905-13/14.

The position is responsible for providing legal advice, and for researching, developing, designing, conducting, delivering and supporting law enforcement training provided by the FLETC to its partner organizations and various other customers.

The position is responsible for conducting a variety of more than 60 basic and advanced legal training courses for law enforcement personnel for numerous Federal Participating Organizations, as well as state and local government entities.

In addition to the training carried out at FLETC, the position may export the courses to on-site locations of the agencies serviced. Typical duties may include: Serving as a senior instructor, subject-matter expert, and program/course developer in the assigned legal program/course areas of law enforcement.

Students in these courses are routinely from the most high-profile law enforcement agencies in the world, including the U.S. Secret Service, the U.S. Marshal's Service, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms, Naval Criminal Investigative Service, Immigration Customs Enforcement, and many others.

The program/courses taught cover subject-matter that involves highly specialized knowledge of complex and difficult legal areas that impact close to 90 Federal agencies that train at the FLETC.

Providing expert training in areas such as: Constitutional Law; Fourth Amendment; Self-Incrimination; Use of Force; Federal Court Procedures; Authority and Jurisdiction; Federal Fraud Statutes; Federal Firearms Violations; Rules of Evidence; Military law; Electronic Law and Evidence; Officer Liability; Criminal Law; Administrative Law; Obstruction of Justice; Terrorism and National Security Law; False Statements; Indian Law; Courtroom Testimony; Assault; Bribery; other emerging areas of the law.

Planning, developing, coordinating, and implementing a legal training program, while balancing the needs and concerns of the DHS training mission. Working with other attorneys, managers and supervisory Federal law enforcement personnel to identify objectives to be met by a specific class.

Selecting appropriate methods, equipment and materials, and developing the courses and providing instruction, guidance and direction to the class in accomplishing specific learning objectives.

Keeping abreast of developing training goals and objectives, and continually restructuring the courses to reflect the current laws, identifying specific areas where study and research is required, searching literature for existing documentation, gathering and analyzing data, producing papers for publication and disseminating for internal use.

Conducting extensive advanced export training (off-site) at other Federal, state, and municipal facilities around the country. Monitoring progress of students, documenting results, and/or recommending remedial and corrective action to include additional training and changes in training and/or operational procedures and instructions.

Evaluates both individual and group performance in various training settings. Overseeing and participating in developing course and program material on the legal aspects of law enforcement.

Initiating content changes and developing different approaches and methods of instruction and recommending any other changes needed to improve the course/program and achieve course/program objectives. View common definitions of terms found in this announcement: Common Definitions.

Required and at times frequent travel to off-site locations to coordinate and/or deliver training activities will be involved. Work also involves considerable physical exertion while demonstrating weapons positions, techniques and tactics in a variety of law enforcement settings.

Work Environment: The normal workplace is a classroom and inside/outside training venues. Duties will require exposure to varying climate and environmental conditions, both cold and warm, for extended periods of time and/or exposure to varying levels of noise and hazardous substances.

Position may be required to drive a government-owned or government-leased vehicle to perform duties at locations on and off-site. Appropriate safety practices will be utilized at all times. Safety equipment, such as hearing and eye protection, will be used when needed.

ThisWay Global, Inc. is an AI-first technology company headquartered in Texas, operating at the intersection of artificial intelligence, data center infrastructure, and workforce solutions. We move fast, work at scale, and are in the middle of several of the most consequential buildouts in the AI infrastructure space right now.

s.h: Our business spans three high-growth areas
s.t:
ADCAP — AI & Data Center Acceleration Platform
ADCAP is a full-lifecycle data center development and operations platform that compresses multi-year build timelines from 36 months down to as little as 14 months. We specialize in site planning, subcontractor vetting, contractor management, and AI workload optimization — and we are currently deploying NVIDIA NVL72/GB300 GPU clusters. This is not theoretical; we are actively building.
Amalgamy.ai — AI Orchestration Software
An enterprise AI orchestration platform that maximizes GPU and compute utilization across complex AI environments, serving large-scale enterprise customers who need to extract every unit of performance from their infrastructure investment.
Staffing & Workforce Solutions
Our foundational business — AI-powered talent matching that connects employers with qualified candidates at scale.
Our CEO, Stephan Fabel, is the former Senior Director of DGX Cloud at NVIDIA. We have a real estate subsidiary, RELLIS DC Real Estate Co., executing a ground lease at the Texas A&M RELLIS campus in the College Station/Bryan area. We are entering complex enterprise, institutional, and government partnerships — and we need a sharp legal mind to help us build the function that supports it all.

This is a ground-floor opportunity. We don't have a legal department — we're building one, and you'll be building it with us. As our first Internal Legal Counsel, you will be a strategic partner to the CEO and executive team, not just a contract reviewer. You will sit at the table for the deals that matter — data center ground leases, AI platform enterprise agreements, TAMU and state entity partnerships, vendor relationships, and everything in between.
This role exists to help ThisWay Global navigate legal, compliance, and operational risk as the business scales across AI, HPC, software, infrastructure, and public-sector partnerships. You will own the legal function end-to-end: drafting, negotiating, advising, and evolving our legal infrastructure as the business scales. Success looks like practical legal guidance, strong risk visibility, scalable processes, and a business team that can move quickly with confidence.
This role is expected to evolve into a broader executive leadership function focused on enterprise risk, governance, compliance, and legal strategy. If you're a talented Texas attorney who has considered a step off the BigLaw path in exchange for equity upside, executive access, and the chance to build something real — this is that role.

Serve as a trusted advisor to the CEO and leadership team; participate in strategic planning, deal structuring, and business development conversations.
Provide practical legal guidance across commercial, operational, and organizational matters; support leadership in balancing risk, speed, and business objectives.
Help build scalable legal and governance processes as the organization grows.
Own the end-to-end lifecycle of commercial contracts, including enterprise SaaS agreements, data center services agreements, vendor contracts, NDAs, subcontractor agreements, and custom deal structures.
Identify legal and operational risks within complex commercial relationships.
Support evolving partnerships across AI, infrastructure, software, and public-sector initiatives.
Support and lead legal work on ground leases, commercial leases, land acquisition, title review, easements, and real estate transactions tied to data center site development, including our RELLIS campus work.
Navigate university, state entity, and government procurement frameworks; structure deals that satisfy both institutional requirements and business objectives.
Advise on employment-related matters, internal policies, and organizational risk.
Support ISO-aligned operational and compliance initiatives.
Partner with leadership on governance, documentation, and internal controls.
Build and maintain our compliance posture across data privacy (GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA awareness), AI and technology regulation, and employment law; flag risks before they become problems.
Help evaluate legal and compliance implications of AI and software deployments; coordinate with technical and operational teams on evolving risk areas.
Establish scalable legal processes, document templates, external counsel relationships, and internal policies; build the function from scratch.
Understand our products well enough to translate AI, data center, and cloud infrastructure concepts into precise legal language.
Help shape a proactive approach to enterprise risk management; identify areas where legal structure, process, or policy can reduce operational exposure.
Contribute to the organization's long-term maturity as legal and compliance needs evolve.

Texas Residency; must be based in Texas (role is remote-first, but Texas presence is required). Some travel to data center sites and university campuses is expected.
5–8 years of experience in a combination of law firm and/or in-house legal roles.

# Legal Counsel im Bereich der Naturwissenschaften (m/w/d) #
Die ETH Zürich ist eine der weltweit führenden technisch-naturwissenschaftlichen Hochschulen. Innerhalb des Vizepräsidiums für Wissenstransfer und Wirtschaftsbeziehungen unterstützt die Forschungsvertragsgruppe Forschende dabei, ihre Projekte mit nationalen und internationalen Partnern auf ein sicheres rechtliches Fundament zu stellen.
Zur Verstärkung unseres Teams suchen wir per sofort oder nach Vereinbarung eine lösungsorientierte Persönlichkeit als Legal Counsel.
## Projekthintergrund ##
**Ihre Rolle an der Schnittstelle zwischen Forschung und Recht**
In dieser Position sind Sie Teil eines kleinen Teams «**Naturwissenschaften**» innerhalb der Forschungsvertragsgruppe und bearbeiten rechtliche Fragen und Verträge für Forschungsprojekte in ausgewählten fachlichen Zuständigkeitsbereichen, insbesondere **Materialwissenschaften, Chemie und Maschinenbau**.

Sie beraten Forschende sowie zentrale Stellen der ETH Zürich und begleiten Projekte an der Schnittstelle von Wissenschaft, Technologieentwicklung und Anwendung.

Dabei arbeiten Sie regelmässig an Vorhaben mit technischem und wirtschaftlichem Bezug, insbesondere im Zusammenhang mit Forschungskooperationen, Industriepartnerschaften, Material- und Technologietransfer sowie projektbezogenen Know-how-Fragestellungen.

Ihre Tätigkeit umfasst die **selbständige Ausarbeitung, Prüfung und Verhandlung von Verträgen** mit nationalen und internationalen Partnern sowie die rechtliche Begleitung komplexer projektbezogener Fragestellungen.
## Stellenbeschreibung ##
**Erarbeitung, Prüfung und Verhandlung von Verträgen** für Forschungsprojekte, insbesondere in den Bereichen Materialwissenschaften, Chemie und Maschinenbau, mit nationalen und internationalen Partnern (z.B. Forschungskooperationen, Industriekooperationen, Materialtransfer, Technologietransfer und Vertraulichkeitsvereinbarungen).
**Beratung und Unterstützung der Forschenden** bei rechtlichen und vertraglichen Fragestellungen im Zusammenhang mit technologieorientierten Forschungsprojekten, insbesondere bei Kooperationen mit Industriepartnern und anderen akademischen Einrichtungen.
**Enge Zusammenarbeit mit zentralen Schnittstellen**, insbesondere dem Rechtsdienst, ETH transfer und weiteren internen Fachstellen, zur Sicherstellung kohärenter rechtlicher Lösungen.
**Koordination mit internen und externen Stakeholdern**, einschliesslich Forschenden, Industriepartnern, Hochschulen, Forschungsinstitutionen und weiteren Projektpartnern.
**Mitwirkung bei der Weiterentwicklung und Standardisierung von Prozessen** für technologieorientierte Forschungsprojekte innerhalb der ETH Zürich, mit Fokus auf effiziente, rechtssichere und praxistaugliche Abläufe.
**Konzeption und Durchführung von Informationsveranstaltungen und Schulungen** für Forschende zu rechtlichen Aspekten von Forschungsverträgen, Industriekooperationen und technologieorientierten Projekten.
**Aktive Mitgestaltung des Vertragsportfolios**, insbesondere in den Bereichen Materialwissenschaften, Chemie und Maschinenbau, innerhalb der Forschungsvertragsgruppe.
## Profil ##
Wir suchen eine integrative Persönlichkeit, die komplexe Sachverhalte schnell durchdringt und Freude an der engen Zusammenarbeit in einem diversen Umfeld hat.
* **Ausbildung:** Sie verfügen über einen Schweizer Hochschulabschluss in Rechtswissenschaften.
**Erfahrung:** Von Vorteil ist Erfahrung in einem industriellen Umfeld oder an der Schnittstelle zwischen Industrie und Hochschule. Idealerweise bringen Sie ein Verständnis dafür mit, wie unterschiedliche Interessen in Forschungskooperationen rechtlich und praktisch zusammengeführt werden können.
* **Kompetenzen:** Sie besitzen ausgezeichnete **analytische und konzeptionelle Fähigkeiten**, **Verhandlungsgeschick** und **Durchsetzungsvermögen** sowie die Fähigkeit, sich schnell in neue Themen einzuarbeiten und flexibel mit **komplexen Sachverhalten** umzugehen. Eine schnelle Auffassungsgabe und ein hohes Mass an **Eigenverantwortung** zeichnen Sie ebenso aus wie eine **effiziente und exakte Arbeitsweise**.
* **Sprachen:** Sie kommunizieren und verhandeln stilsicher in **Deutsch **und **Englisch **(Wort und Schrift). Französischkenntnisse sind von Vorteil.
* **Mindset:** Sie arbeiten **effizient, exakt** und **lösungsorientiert** und verfügen über einen ausgeprägten **Team**geist und hohe **Sozialkompetenz**. Sie verfügen über das im Drittmittelwesen einer Hochschule notwendige Gespür, wo Wissenschaftler **rasch** und **pragmatisch** unterstützt werden müssen.
Durch das Formulieren von klaren und eindeutigen vertraglichen Regelungen legen Sie die Basis für die spätere praktische Umsetzung der Forschungsergebnisse. Sie sind in der Lage, ein **heterogenes Portfolio an Geschäften eigenständig zu organisieren** und termingerecht zu erledigen. Indem Sie zügig, lösungsorientiert und umsichtig arbeiten, ermöglichen Sie den Forschenden die Durchführung ihrer exzellenten Projekte.
Wenn Sie darüber hinaus Interesse an naturwissenschaftlichen, technischen und wirtschaftlichen Zusammenhängen haben, bringen Sie ideale Voraussetzungen mit.
Werden Sie Teil der ETH Zürich, die nicht nur Ihre berufliche Entwicklung unterstützt, sondern auch aktiv zu positiven Veränderungen in der Gesellschaft beiträgt. Wir engagieren uns für eine nachhaltige und klimaneutrale Hochschule.
## Wir bieten ##

* Zahlreiche Vergünstigungen, wie z.B. ÖV-Abonnemente und Car Sharing, ein breites Sportangebot des ASVZ, Kinderbetreuung sowie attraktive Vorsorgeleistungen;
* Flexibles Arbeiten und Möglichkeit für Homeoffice.

## Diversität und Nachhaltigkeit sind uns wichtig ##
Im Einklang mit unseren Werten unterstützt die ETH Zürich eine inklusive Kultur. Wir fördern Chancengleichheit, schätzen Vielfalt und pflegen ein Arbeits- und Lernumfeld, in dem die Rechte und die Würde aller Mitarbeitenden und Studierenden respektiert werden.

Auf unserer Webseite zur Chancengleichheit und Vielfalt erfahren Sie, wie wir ein faires und offenes Umfeld sicherstellen, in dem sich alle entwickeln und entfalten können. Nachhaltigkeit ist für uns ein zentraler Wert - wir arbeiten konsequent an einer klimaneutralen Zukunft.

Provide expert, authoritative advice and counsel to the ODNI General Counsel and senior leadership and staff on often complex, difficult, and novel legal issues (1) that affect the responsibilities of the DNI and ODNI as they relate to statutes, Presidential directives, Executive Orders, and other related laws and policies, including the DNI's statutory responsibility to ensure compliance with the Constitution and laws of the United States by elements of the IC; and (2) that relate to all aspects of intelligence law and federal agency law, to include collection, analysis, covert action, foreign relations, intelligence and information sharing, security and protection of sources and methods, intelligence policy and legislation, and other related areas of intelligence and national security law, intelligence community policies and legislation, administrative law, personnel law, government ethics, government information practices, acquisition and procurement law, and federal appropriations law.

Render legal opinions and associated oral advice on a wide range of issues, often in areas where few or no legal precedents exist, and ensure legal requirements are implemented across the IC.

Research and analyze a wide variety of laws, regulations, legislation, and policies; and draft or review new legislation (to include the annual Intelligence Authorization Act), Executive Orders, policies, congressional testimony, and related policy guidance.

Supervise and manage a team of attorneys and staff, including assisting with the supervision of other managers and the management of the OGC, including the development of the OGC budget, the approval of leave and training requests, the distribution of portfolios and assignments, the HR process, and other general office management issues.

Establish and manage liaison relationships with external partners to ensure a comprehensive and coordinated approach to intelligence and national security law topics. Represent the General Counsel and the ODNI on a variety of intra- and inter-agency committees and working groups.

s.h: POSITION SUMMARY - RENEWABLE ENERGY SENIOR CORPORATE ATTORNEY
s.t:
Clean Energy Counsel , a mission-driven law firm dedicated to accelerating the world’s transition away from fossil fuels, seeks to hire a highly qualified senior corporate associate with excellent law firm experience and academic credentials to join our firm. This attorney will advise clean energy companies, project developers, investors, private equity funds, and other clients on a broad range of sophisticated corporate and transactional matters.
The ideal candidate will have substantial experience handling complex business transactions and will be comfortable taking a lead role in client relationships, negotiations, and transaction execution. Experience in the clean energy, renewable energy, infrastructure, climate technology, or sustainable development sectors is mandatory.
This is an opportunity to join a collaborative, mission-driven law firm and work directly with sophisticated clients on transactions that support the continued growth of the clean energy economy.
This position is fully remote – as a distributed law firm, we offer the opportunity to work remotely from wherever you are licensed to practice law.

5+ years of experience at a law firm, ideally in a practice serving clients in the renewable energy and related industries.
Demonstrated experience leading or substantially contributing to complex financing, joint venture, private equity, or other strategic transactions.
Strong drafting, negotiation, analytical, and client-management skills. Ability to confidently and competently serve as the senior, lead attorney on complex financing transactions, including management of the deal and supporting attorney team(s) with minimal oversight.
Strong organization, drafting, communication, negotiation, and analytical skills.
Team-focused outlook with a focus on mentoring junior attorneys.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills as well as organizational, planning, and project management skills with the capacity to simultaneously handle a variety of complex matters under strict deadlines and pressure.
Ability to work and collaborate effectively in a remote work environment.
Admission to and in good standing with the Bar of the applicant’s state of residence.
Dedication to the firm’s mission.

Advise clients on complex corporate and transactional matters throughout the business lifecycle.
Lead and support reorganizations, restructurings, and other corporate strategic transactions.
Structure and negotiate equity financings, private equity investments, and other capital-raising transactions.
Structure and negotiate joint ventures, strategic partnerships, and other commercial arrangements.
Advise clients on corporate governance, entity formation, capitalization, shareholder and partnership matters, and related corporate issues.
Adhere to Firm policies, practices, and priorities.
Identify legal and business risks and develop practical, creative solutions that advance clients’ objectives.
Supervise and mentor junior attorneys and other members of deal teams.
Contribute to the development of CEC’s corporate practice, including identifying opportunities to expand client relationships and generate new business.
Stay current on legal, regulatory, and market developments affecting corporate transactions and the clean energy industry.

1,200 annual billable hour requirement, with bonuses for exceeding such requirement and for origination of new clients and matters based on a percentage of total revenue received.
Base salary of $220,000+. The base salary for this position will be determined during the interview process and will vary based on multiple factors, including but not limited to prior experience, relevant expertise, current business needs, and market factors.

For clients, this translates to an extraordinary level of care, brought to bear for common cause. As the only mission-driven law firm solely focused on renewable energy, Clean Energy Counsel carries forward its unique model of advancing a sustainable future with sustainable law.
Our singular focus attracts the best talent in the industry, and we’ve built a deep and diverse bench of industry veterans who are passionate about their work and value our culture of respect and support.
We represent a diverse range of renewable energy project developers, investors, suppliers, and service providers across a full spectrum of technologies, including solar, energy storage, wind, energy efficiency, electric vehicles and charging infrastructure, waste to value, and sustainable infrastructure and materials - from Fortune 50 companies to start-ups.

Our deep-rooted commitment to diversity and inclusion drives our ability to attract high-performing attorneys with diverse experience and perspectives who value a supportive work culture based on care and respect.

Le SCCO, qui compte environ 150 collaborateurs·trices, regroupe des entités responsables de taxer et percevoir différents impôts. L'entité juridique du service a pour mission principale d'apporter le soutien juridique à l'ensemble du service. Elle établit également les observations dans le cadre des procédures de recours auprès des tribunaux. Elle traite les procédures d'exonération et d'assujettissement. Elle rédige les projets de lois et règlements relevant de la législation fiscale cantonale.
Vos missions
En qualité de juriste au sein du service des contributions, vous traitez des procédures d’assujettissement de personnes physiques et morales, ainsi que des procédures d’exonération de personnes morales. L'instruction de ces dossiers ainsi que la rédaction de décisions rythment votre quotidien, tout comme vos échanges avec les contribuables et les différentes autorités fiscales cantonales.
Dans le cadre de procédures de recours au Tribunal cantonal et au Tribunal fédéral, vous êtes en charge de rédiger des observations.
Votre expertise profite également au personnel du service, que vous soutenez dans la résolution de problématiques juridiques soulevées lors de l'analyse de leurs dossiers. Vous participez, par ailleurs, à l'élaboration et à l'actualisation des directives internes et externes en matière d'assujettissement et d'exonération, ainsi qu'à la formation interne.
Votre profil
Vous êtes titulaire d'un master en droit et portez un intérêt particulier à la fiscalité. À l'aise avec vos interlocuteurs·trices et doté·e d'un esprit d'analyse et de synthèse, vous savez aussi bien prendre qu'assumer vos décisions.
Vous maîtrisez parfaitement l'orthographe et la langue française ainsi que les outils informatiques usuels.
Autonome, vous vous distinguez par votre conscience professionnelle et faites preuve d'initiative dans le respect des compétences attribuées. La précision et le sérieux caractérisent votre travail, même en période de forte sollicitation.

The Associate General Counsel serves as a strategic legal advisor to business leaders across the company, providing practical guidance on complex commercial, operational, and regulatory matters.

This role requires substantial independent judgment to manage significant legal projects, lead high-value negotiations and cross-functional initiatives, develop scalable legal processes, and partner closely with executive leadership to support business growth while managing commercial, financial, operational, and reputational risk.
What Will You Be Doing?
Draft, review, and negotiate complex commercial agreements (partnerships, licensing, manufacturing, distribution, MSAs, technology, vendor/supplier arrangements, leases, and capital improvement and operational services contracts), independently managing high-value matters from inception through resolution.
Serve as a trusted legal advisor to business units and senior leadership, partnering cross-functionally to identify risks, develop practical solutions, and support strategic initiatives.
Advise on domestic and international operations, including sourcing, supply chain, logistics, freight and shipping, manufacturing, distribution, cross-border trade, import/export compliance, and government relations.
Provide legal counsel on domestic and international strategic business transactions, including investments, financings, joint ventures, acquisitions, and corporate restructurings, from initial evaluation and due diligence through execution, coordinating with outside counsel as needed.
Lead complex cross-functional projects such as new market entry, product launches, and operational expansions, coordinating legal input across subject areas.
Manage disputes, investigations, claims, and pre-litigation matters; oversee outside counsel relationships, legal budgets, and efficient use of legal resources.
Advise on employment and labor matters, including employee relations, workplace policies, wage and hour compliance, leave administration, employment-related disputes, and management of employment litigation and agency proceedings.
Advise on commercial credit operations, including customer credit policies, risk assessment frameworks, secured transactions, and management of collections and recovery matters.
Oversee corporate governance, entity formation and maintenance, subsidiary management, and organizational structuring matters.
Advise on intellectual property, branding, marketing, advertising, and product commercialization initiatives, as well as data privacy, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and other technology-related matters.
Advise on product safety and regulatory compliance across federal, state, and international requirements, and monitor relevant legal developments.
Build and maintain contract templates, negotiation playbooks, legal policies, and operational best practices; lead process improvement initiatives and deliver training designed to improve scalability, efficiency, and risk management across the organization.
Comply with all policies and standards.

Juris Doctor (JD) from an accredited law school and active bar membership in good standing
7-9 years of corporate legal experience
Licensed Attorney (varies by state)
Strong foundation in drafting, reviewing, and negotiating complex commercial agreements, including licensing, manufacturing, distribution, and technology arrangements
Experience managing disputes, investigations, and outside counsel relationships
Familiarity with employment and labor law, including employee relations, workplace investigations, and employment-related disputes
Background in corporate governance and entity management
Track record of building scalable legal processes, templates, playbooks, or training programs is preferred
Experience with international operations, cross-border transactions, trade compliance, customs, import/export regulations, supply chain, government relations, or cross-border regulatory matters is a meaningful plus.
Ability to translate complex legal issues into practical business guidance
Comfortable working independently, exercising substantial judgment on high-value matters, and managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
Strong communicator who builds trust with business partners across all levels of the organization
Experience in the apparel, retail, wholesale, or consumer products industry is preferred but not required. Exposure to intellectual property, data privacy, technology transactions, product regulatory matters, or corporate transactions (M&A, investments, restructurings) is a plus

* Vous préparez les négociations avec les cantons, les communes, les particuliers et d'autres entreprises, et accompagnez les partenaires internes lors de leur conduite.
* Dans le cadre d'études et de projets des CFF, vous analysez les mesures contractuelles nécessaires, conseillez les directions de projet et accompagnez la mise en œuvre des contrats requis.
* Vous participez à des groupes spécialisés traitant de sujets transversaux, par exemple l'élaboration et le développement de bases contractuelles et de processus ainsi que les questions de principe relatives aux voies de raccordement. De plus, vous assurez la suppléance de vos collègues en cas d'absence et garantissez la continuité du traitement des affaires en cours.
Ce que vous apportez.

De plus, vous faites preuve d'assurance, d'habileté dans la négociation, d'initiative ainsi que d'une méthode de travail rigoureuse et fiable.
* Vous maîtrisez les applications Microsoft Office usuelles et vous vous familiarisez rapidement avec de nouveaux systèmes et processus.
* Vous disposez d'une formation professionnelle commerciale ou d'une formation comparable ainsi que de plusieurs années d'expérience. Une expérience dans le domaine ferroviaire, des infrastructures, de l'immobilier ou de la gestion contractuelle constitue un avantage.

* Pour un engagement direct en qualité de spécialiste contrats, vous disposez idéalement d'une formation supérieure ou d'un diplôme d'une haute école ainsi que d'une solide expérience dans le traitement autonome de questions contractuelles, juridiques ou infrastructurelles complexes.

About Alta Ares
Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them.
Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.
Founded in 2024, we have grown to 90 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development.
Role & Mission
As Legal & IP Counsel, you will be Alta Ares' first dedicated in-house legal hire responsible for building and managing the company's legal function across three core pillars: intellectual property, commercial contracts, and corporate law.
You will work directly with the CEO and COO on the legal dimensions of Alta Ares' most consequential decisions: protecting the IP that underpins our technology, structuring commercial agreements with defence clients and institutional partners, and ensuring the company's corporate and regulatory foundations are solid as we scale internationally.
This is a builder role. You will establish processes, templates, and legal infrastructure from scratch in a fast-moving environment where precision, speed, and discretion are non-negotiable. You will work across multiple jurisdictions (France, UK, US, Ukraine) and across a highly sensitive sector where legal rigour directly impacts national security.
1. Intellectual Property
Own Alta Ares' IP strategy and portfolio: patents, trade secrets, software copyrights, and know-how protection across all product lines (ISR, C-UAS, MLOps, HSI)
Lead patent filing processes in coordination with external patent attorneys: drafting invention disclosures, managing prosecution, and maintaining the patent portfolio
Define and enforce IP protection policies internally: employee IP assignment, contractor IP clauses, and open-source usage governance
Conduct IP due diligence on partnerships, licensing arrangements, and potential acquisitions
Monitor the competitive IP landscape and flag freedom-to-operate risks proactively
Advise Engineering and Product teams on IP-sensitive design decisions and open-source compliance
2. Commercial Contracts & Defence Agreements
Draft, review, and negotiate all commercial agreements: customer contracts, MOUs, teaming agreements, NDAs, subcontracting arrangements, and licensing agreements
Own the contract management lifecycle: template creation, negotiation support, execution tracking, and renewals
Advise on the legal specificities of defence procurement contracts across multiple jurisdictions: French DGA, NATO, EU institutions, UK MOD, and US DoD frameworks
Review and negotiate grant agreements under EU defence funding mechanisms: EDF, EUDIS, Horizon Europe
Manage and mitigate contractual risk in multi-party, multi-jurisdiction arrangements
Build and maintain a library of standardised contract templates adapted to Alta Ares' commercial contexts
3. Corporate Law & Regulatory Compliance
Support the legal structuring and maintenance of Alta Ares' multi-entity corporate architecture: France (SAS), UK (Ltd), US (Inc.), Ukraine, and any future entities
Advise on corporate governance matters: board resolutions, shareholder agreements, equity plan (BSPCE) documentation, and cap table management in coordination with Finance
Manage regulatory compliance across applicable frameworks: RGPD/GDPR, French corporate law, and sector-specific defence regulations
Support export control compliance across applicable regimes: French AECA / CIEEMG, ITAR, EAR, and dual-use regulation in coordination with the RSSI and Sales teams
Assist in fundraising processes: term sheet review, investor documentation, and legal due diligence responses
Liaise with external counsel across jurisdictions and manage external legal spend efficiently
4. Legal Advisory & Internal Counsel
Serve as the go-to legal advisor for all teams: Sales, Engineering, HR, Finance, and Operations
Provide rapid, practical legal guidance on day-to-day questions balancing legal rigour with business pragmatism
Flag and escalate legal risks proactively to the CEO and COO
Maintain organised legal documentation and contract registers in Notion
Contribute to the development of internal policies with legal dimensions: data protection, security, and compliance frameworks
Candidate Profile
Experience
3 years of experience in law combining in-house counsel experience and/or private practice in a top-tier firm
Strong background in at least two of: intellectual property law, commercial contracts, corporate law
Exposure to technology, deeptech, defence, aerospace, or dual-use sectors is a strong plus
Experience working with or within a startup or scale-up is a significant advantage: you understand the pace and constraints of a lean legal function
Prior exposure to multi-jurisdictional legal environments (France + UK or US) is valued
Familiarity with French corporate law (SAS governance, BSPCE, equity documentation) is a plus
Skills & Qualities
French fluency is mandatory : primary legal and corporate jurisdiction is France
English fluency is mandatory : commercial agreements, international partnerships, and investor documentation are predominantly in English
Rigorous and detail-oriented, you catch what others miss and never cut corners on substance
Pragmatic and business-minded: you give clear, actionable legal advice, not just risk catalogues
Fast and responsive in a defence startup, legal bottlenecks have operational consequences
Proactive: you anticipate legal issues before they become problems
Discreet and trustworthy you handle the company's most sensitive commercial, financial, and strategic information
Comfortable operating as a generalist in a lean environment where scope is broad and resources are limited

The Assistant Chief Counsel executes these duties and responsibilities through a geographically dispersed organization of approximately 30 managers, attorneys, and support professionals.

Principal Duties and Responsibilities: Provides executive leadership and strategic oversight of FAA regulatory law programs, directing the planning, policy development, and execution of legal activities and ensuring legal sufficiency and alignment with the priorities of the President, DOT Secretary, FAA Administrator, and Chief Counsel.

Renders authoritative legal opinions and interpretations of FAA regulatory law programs and policies, ensuring consistency with applicable Federal statutes, Executive Orders, and Department of Transportation and FAA policies.

Oversees the delivery of regulatory law services across FAA headquarters and regional offices, including legal support for litigation involving FAA regulatory activities, training, policy development, and evaluation of legal services.

Serves as a senior regulatory law advisor and subject matter expert to FAA and external stakeholders, providing strategic legal advice and counsel to executives at FAA, the Department of Transportation, other Federal agencies, Congress, and private-sector stakeholders on matters affecting FAA regulatory programs.

Leads and manages the Regulations Division, establishing objectives and strategies; directing subordinate managers, attorneys, and staff; allocating resources and workload; evaluating performance; making personnel decisions; and fostering organizational effectiveness.
